disturbances.detail: server killed hard while the journey was running; the next cycle passed without help

disturbances.name: outbox drains after the server restart
disturbances.detail: no event stayed Pending after the restart
measures: 4 event(s) in the outbox, 0 Pending at the moment of the kill, 0 Pending for over a minute afterwards

disturbances.name: token and rate-limiter key churn
disturbances.detail: memory plateaued: +26112 KB over the first two rounds, +4464 KB over the last two (cap 65536 KB)
measures: 4000 junk-token and 4000 signed-token requests per round, 4 rounds; 8100 answered, 7900 rate-limited
server RSS KB: before 39392, after round 1 57544, after round 2 65504, after rounds 3-4 69968

disturbances.name: database restart
disturbances.detail: Postgres restarted (fast) under load, server kept running; service resumed without a server restart

disturbances.name: month boundary and time zone (database level)
disturbances.detail: the business day starts at the same instant whichever zone the session uses, and the day before ends one second earlier; running the application at a faked date still needs a clock seam
measures: 19 boundary checks over 6 dates and 3 session zones, plus one daylight-saving business-zone check

disturbances.name: import killed while it checks its rows
disturbances.detail: server killed hard while the import checked its rows; the restarted server carried it on by itself and it ended as a run with no crash
measures: healthy again after 0.5 s; the check carried on by itself and ended 394 s after the kill
committed and reconciled 50 s after approval

disk_projection_24h.basis: linear extrapolation of the measured window at the same load; real growth bends with retention, vacuum and load

command_for_24h_run: journeylab soak -duration 24h -server-bin <server> -pg-bin <pg bin dir> -out <dir>   (needs the same JWT_SECRET exported as the soak uses; see the guide)
limits: the time-zone check is a database check: there is no application clock seam, so the app itself cannot be run at a faked date
the limiter check watches the server's memory; the limiter's own table size is not exposed
the soak runs on one machine, so server and database share its CPU and disk
disk projection is linear from this run's measured growth at this load
